title: SSE mid-stream schema negotiation and tool-call handoff for legacy client compatibility
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Problem: Customers increasingly rely on function/tool calling and structured JSON outputs streamed over SSE. Legacy clients expect stable newline/JSONL boundaries and cannot tolerate unexpected mid-stream schema changes. We need a server-side protocol for negotiating and signaling schema/format transitions mid-stream, a deterministic handoff for function-call frames to downstream tool-runner services, and backward-compatible shims for EventSource-based consumers. Scope: define wire-level sentinel events, a compact mid-stream manifest (schemaDelta), deterministic tool-call frame encapsulation that preserves idempotency, and an opt-in compatibility mode that emits legacy-compatible JSONL snapshots on reconnect. Out of scope: wholesale redesign of client SDKs; on-device runtime changes for private deployments (handled in follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Server emits explicit 'schemaDelta' SSE events when the output schema changes mid-stream and includes a stable schema version identifier and a minimal JSON Schema diff string.

2) Function/tool calls must be framed as atomic SSE events with 'tool-call-start' and 'tool-call-end' markers and an embedded idempotency token; replays after reconnect must not re-execute side-effectful tools if the token was acknowledged.

3) Legacy EventSource clients in compatibility mode receive periodic newline-delimited JSONL 'snapshot' events and a final 'stream-end-snapshot' that contains the latest structured output for rehydration on reconnect.

4) Reconnect behavior: clients can supply a reconnect-seq token; server will honor it to resume from last acknowledged top-level event boundary or provide a graceful fallback snapshot if gaps are detected.
5) Tooling: provide test harness with simulated lossy connections, verify idempotency tokens prevent double-invocation, and publish interop tests for at least two major browser EventSource behaviors.
6) Documented rollout plan and compatibility toggle: default enabled for new model variants; explicit header X-Redwood-Stream-Compat: legacy to enable JSONL snapshots for existing customers.
notes: Design trade-off: embedding full JSON Schema for every delta increases bytes; instead we version schemas and send compact diffs. Keep full schema optional behind a feature flag.
We prefer server-side determination of tool-call atomicity to avoid client mis-framing; clients still must include call metadata and an idempotency token generated client-side.
Fallback snapshot frequency set to 30s by default with jitter to reduce synchronized spikes across clients.
Security: schemaDelta events do not contain PII; tool-call payloads must be encrypted in transit and logged with redaction markers in observability.
Performance: ensure delta emission does not increase mean latency by more than 3ms p95; add microbenchmarking in runtime-1.22 branch.
